title: Structure à l'infini des Mg,ν [pages 1 à 90, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Grothendieck is building the combinatorics of the stratification at infinity of the moduli spaces M̄_{g,ν}. An 'MD-graph' (Mumford–Deligne graph) is the dual graph of a stable ν-pointed curve. It consists of:
- a vertex set S;
- half-edges ('arcs') Ã with a fixed-point-free involution σ;
- legs (marked points) I → S;
- a genus function g: S → ℕ.
It must be connected and satisfy the stability condition 2g_β + (valence incl. legs) ≥ 3.

A 'generalized morphism' of graphs f: G' → G sends vertices to vertices and arcs either to arcs or to identities of Π_1(G), i.e. arcs may be contracted. B̃' ⊂ Ã' denotes the arcs not contracted. G'(α) is the fibre subgraph over a vertex α ∈ S: the vertices S'_α over α and the contracted arcs between them, with external valence B̃'_α ∪ I'_α.

The page states (48): such an f corresponds to a 'morphism of generization' (with a suitable identification I' ≃ I of legs) iff three conditions hold.
1°) Combinatorial conditions:
  - S' → S is surjective;
  - B̃' → Ã is bijective;
  - every fibre graph G'(α) is connected.
  He remarks these do not depend on the MD-structures (genera, legs).
2°) Leg count: ν_α = card I_α = Σ_{β∈S'_α} card I'_β. This depends only on the marked weights and on S' → S.
3°) Genus: g_α = Σ_{β∈S'_α} g'_β + h_1(G'(α)).
A fourth condition, stability of each fibre graph (2g'_β + card I'_β + card B̃'_β ≥ 3), is crossed out. Presumably it is redundant or not intended here; the previous page derives fibre stability from G' being an MD-graph.

In modern terms this is the standard notion of a morphism of stable graphs given by contracting a set of edges, B' being the complement. Such a morphism corresponds to the inclusion of a boundary stratum Δ_{G'} into the closure of a less degenerate stratum Δ_G of M̄_{g,ν}. Contracting a connected subgraph replaces it by one vertex whose genus is the sum of the genera plus the first Betti number of the subgraph, and whose legs are inherited.

The next page goes on to show that G and f are determined up to isomorphism by G' and the set B' of non-contracted edges (S ≃ π_0 of the contracted subgraph, Ã ≃ B̃').
errors: No mathematical error. Condition 2° is essentially automatic once the leg bijection I' ≃ I is required to be compatible with S' → S. He lists it to separate it from the purely graph-theoretic condition 1°.
The struck-out condition 4° reflects hesitation about whether stability of the fibre graphs needs to be imposed; it is implied by stability of G' (as noted on the previous page).

ideas.what: Characterization of edge-contraction morphisms between stable (Mumford–Deligne) graphs by surjectivity on vertices, bijectivity on surviving half-edges, connected fibres, additivity of legs, and the genus formula g_α = Σ g'_β + h_1(fibre)
ideas.modern_name: Morphisms (contractions) of stable graphs; the specialization poset of strata of M̄_{g,n}
ideas.usually_credited_to: Implicit in Deligne–Mumford (1969) and Knudsen; made explicit by Arbarello–Cornalba (1990s) and Getzler–Kapranov (1998, modular operads)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme discusses the 'structure à l'infini' of M_{g,ν} and the Teichmüller tower informally, but not this graph formalism

ideas.what: Recovering the generized graph G from G' and a σ-stable subset B' of edges (S ≃ π_0 of the contracted subgraph) — continued on the next page
ideas.modern_name: Edge contraction G'/E determined by the contracted edge set
ideas.usually_credited_to: standard graph theory / folklore in moduli of curves

deep.surprise_reason: This is a careful but standard formalization of the contraction morphisms of dual graphs of stable curves, now textbook material (Arbarello–Cornalba–Griffiths, Getzler–Kapranov). It is of historical interest as Grothendieck's own early formalism ('MD-graphs', 'morphismes de générisation'), but nothing on it is mathematically new.
transcription_corrections: Line 1: 'morphisme générateur de graphes' should read 'morphisme généralisé de graphes' (consistent with the next page, 'morphisme généralisé de graphes ordinaires').
In 1°, the closing quotation mark should be after 'graphes fibres': 'les "graphes fibres" G'(α) (α∈S) connexes'.
In 2°, the underbraces are ν_α under card I_α and ν'_β under card I'_β; this is correct as transcribed.

The struck-out 4° reads approximately: '∀ α' ∈ S', on a (non seulement 2g'_{α'} + card I'_{α'} + card Ã'_{α'} ≥ 3, mais même) 2g'_{α'} + card I'_{α'} + card B̃'_{α'} ≥ 3'. The index in the first inequality should be α' rather than β'.
